story.title: Six People Die in Plane Crash Off Mississippi Coast
story.summary: A small plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi, resulting in the deaths of all six passengers, including two children aged 10 and 12. The plane was traveling from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida, when it lost contact with air traffic control. The Coast Guard has recovered the bodies, and an investigation into the cause of the crash is underway.

explore_lenses.label: Who was aboard, and why did details change?
explore_lenses.title: Officials corrected early passenger information
explore_lenses.summary: Updated reporting identifies the victims as six members of two Fort Myers-area families returning from a fishing trip. The correction matters because early Coast Guard-based accounts understated the number of children aboard.

claims.text: Jackson County Coroner Bruce Lynd Jr. identified the victims as pilot Brent Stokes, his 16-year-old son Hunter, Arlyn and Michael Knox, and their sons Charles Holden Knox, 12, and Truett Knox, 10.
The Associated Press reported that it corrected earlier information after the coroner’s office said there were three boys aboard, including the 16-year-old, rather than two.
The Knox and Stokes families said the group had been on a fishing trip and was heading home to be with family for the holiday season.

The Knox and Stokes families said the group had been on a fishing trip and was heading home to be with family for the holiday season.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Authorities have identified the victims, but public reporting does not establish who was operating the aircraft at the moment it went down beyond identifying Stokes as the pilot.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the investigation?
explore_lenses.title: NTSB evidence review will determine cause
explore_lenses.summary: The FAA and NTSB are investigating, with the NTSB expected to assemble factual evidence before issuing any probable-cause finding. The first public investigative product is likely to be factual rather than a conclusion about blame or cause.

claims.text: The FAA and NTSB are investigating the crash, according to reporting based on agency information.
The NTSB says it does not determine cause while at the scene; its general-aviation process includes on-scene fact gathering, later analysis, and a final report that states probable cause.
Forecast: Under the NTSB’s stated general-aviation process, a preliminary factual report is typically available within about two weeks, while a final report commonly takes roughly 18 to 24 months.
The NTSB says accident dockets can include items such as records, photographs, and witness information, and may be released during the investigation or at its conclusion.

story_report.summary: Six people, including two children, died when a plane crashed off Mississippi’s coast while en route from New Orleans to Fort Myers, Florida. The Coast Guard recovered the bodies, and authorities are investigating the crash. The victims included pilot Brent Stokes and members of the Knox family, who relatives said had been returning home after a fishing trip for the holiday season.

sections.heading: Victims Identified by Coroner
sections.body: Jackson County Coroner Bruce Lynd Jr. identified the dead as Stokes; his 16-year-old son, Hunter; Arlyn and Michael Knox; and the Knoxes’ sons, Charles Holden Knox, 12, and Truett Knox, 10. The Associated Press corrected earlier reporting after the coroner’s office said three boys, including the 16-year-old, were aboard rather than two.

sections.heading: Federal Agencies Examine Crash
sections.body: The Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board are investigating. The NTSB says its general-aviation inquiries begin with on-scene fact gathering and proceed through analysis to a final report stating probable cause; its dockets can include records, photographs and witness information. Under the agency’s general timetable, a preliminary factual report is typically available in about two weeks and a final report commonly takes 18 to 24 months.

unresolved.text: No public preliminary report or probable-cause finding had been located as of Nov. 25, 2026; the NTSB’s published investigation timetable is a general expectation rather than a case-specific schedule.
Public reporting does not establish who was operating the aircraft when it went down, beyond identifying Brent Stokes as the pilot.

related_stories.title: Dozens Killed in Cairo Highway Fire Following Fuel Tanker Crash
related_stories.summary: A fuel tanker crash on a major highway surrounding Cairo has resulted in at least 30 fatalities and 15 injuries. The vehicle, carrying petroleum products, reportedly overturned and ignited a massive fire, leading to a significant emergency response. Authorities have indicated that the death toll may rise as investigations continue.

related_stories.summary: Two men have been charged with burglary and trespassing following a break-in at the Sandringham Estate, the Norfolk residence of the Prince and Princess of Wales. During the incident, cufflinks and a clock were reported stolen. The men appeared in court to face the charges.

related_stories.title: Russian Strikes Kill Seven in Ukraine; Kyiv Targets Refineries
related_stories.summary: Russian drone attacks resulted in the deaths of seven people across six Ukrainian regions, targeting infrastructure including a gas production facility and a thermal power plant. In response, Ukraine launched drone strikes on Russian oil refineries in the Samara and Rostov regions, as well as an airbase in Nizhny Novgorod, leading to at least one reported death in the Samara region.
